# Documentation update + full-suite verification

Final task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC6, AC7).

## Goal

Document the shared mineral kill-drop code in the GDD and confirm the whole project is green.

## Minimal implementation

- Update `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.1 to state that the kill-drop rule (small-asteroid single drop; non-asteroid 25–50 % re-drop) is implemented once in a shared helper used by both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`.
- Update §6.4's `GymMinerals` entry (and any relevant file-breakdown lines) to reflect the shared helper and the wired drop behaviour.
- Update `README.md` if it references the mineral layer.
- Run the full suite plus typecheck/build; triage any failure through the triage skill.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC6 — Documentation updated.** The GDD (§4.4.1 and §6.4) and the gym docstrings describe the shared mineral kill-drop code.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** `npm test` (the full suite) passes and `npm run typecheck` succeeds.
- The GDD §6.4 `GymMinerals` entry and any `README.md` mineral wording are consistent with the wired gym behaviour.
- `npm run build` succeeds and no balance or tuning values are changed.

## Key Files

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4.1, §6.4.
- `README.md` — if it references minerals.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — docstrings.

data.description:
# Thruster hum Tone.js shim

## Goal

Implement the continuous, thrust-driven thruster hum as a lightweight Tone.js runtime shim, since baked WAV variants cannot reproduce a pitch/gain-continuous, thrust-coupled loop.

As the game's developer, I want the thruster hum to remain continuous and thrust-driven, so the tuning slider stays audible and the hum stays in lockstep with the flame animation.

## Scope

- Add a small Tone.js-based runtime shim that owns only the thruster hum; all other cues are baked assets (decision recorded on the parent epic).
- Preserve the existing `updateThrusterSound(level)` / `stopThrusterSound()` contract consumed by `Player.preUpdate`.
- Reproduce the documented character: triangle fundamental ~60 Hz + sine undertone ~35 Hz + band-pass filtered noise (700–1100 Hz) whoosh, gain ≤ 0.075.
- Mirror the flame growth/shrink timing (30 ms growth, ~4x decay) and avoid clicks on retrigger.
- Stop cleanly on release, respawn, player destroy and scene shutdown so no audio nodes leak.
- Degrade to a safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- Add Tone.js as a pinned runtime dependency and verify it is the only new browser runtime dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The thruster hum is continuous while thrust is held and stops cleanly on release/respawn/destroy/scene shutdown.
- Hum gain tracks `getEngineSoundLevel` and stays ≤ 0.075.
- No clicks on retrigger; growth/decay match the documented flame timing.
- The shim is a safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- No audio nodes leak after repeated thrust start/stop cycles (asserted in tests).
- Tone.js is pinned and is the only new browser runtime dependency introduced.
- `npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass.

## Dependencies

- Audio playback contract tests.
- Rewrite effects.ts to Phaser playback.

## Deliverables

- Thruster hum shim module.
- Wiring from `updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound` to the shim.
- Shim tests covering continuous gain tracking, clean stop and no-op degradation.

## Key Files

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound` delegate here.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — per-frame driver.
- `src/core/movement.ts` — `getEngineSoundLevel` source.
- `package.json` — Tone.js dependency.
data.title: Thruster hum Tone.js shim

# Update audio documentation

## Goal

Update the game's audio documentation to describe the ToneForge-based baked-asset pipeline, replacing the "zero external audio assets" stance and the procedural-synthesis descriptions.

As the game's developer, I want the docs to describe the ToneForge pipeline accurately, so future audio work starts from the shipped design.

## Scope

- Update GDD §7.3 to state the baked-WAV + ToneForge methodology, the thruster-hum runtime shim exception, and the build-time generation requirement.
- Preserve the SFX event catalogue, per-enemy audio character and player audio character tables, re-pointing synthesis references to recipe names where available.
- Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` per-enemy audio ownership to reference ToneForge recipe slugs.
- Update the audio-directory tree note to describe `public/audio/sfx/` and `scripts/build-audio.sh`.
- Record the recipe-to-cue mapping in the docs (or link to it) so docs and code cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- GDD §7.3 describes the ToneForge baked-asset pipeline and no longer mandates "zero external audio assets".
- GDD §7.3 documents the thruster-hum runtime shim as the single runtime-synthesised exception.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` references ToneForge recipe names for per-enemy audio.
- The audio-directory tree note describes `public/audio/sfx/` and the build script.
- Documentation links the recipe-to-cue mapping so it is discoverable.
- No documentation still claims procedural Web Audio synthesis is the shipping approach.

## Dependencies

- Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit.
- Author game-specific ToneForge recipes.

## Deliverables

- Updated `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3.
- Updated `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` audio sections.
- Updated audio-directory tree note.

## Key Files

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 Audio Direction.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — per-enemy audio ownership.
data.title: Update audio documentation
